title: Started to work on local offline solution for creating 3D assets
author: LegendaryJohnny
selftext:
Creating every asset by prompting Claude would be ineffective in long term, paying for Meshy is also not great option. So last few days I am trying to figure out how to solve this problem. And I told myself why not to create all tools for videogame assets with Claude, which will save for Usage in long term?

And first results are surprisingly good. I now have a tool which can create 3D meshes very well. The only problem to solve are textures now. I asked claude to design feature which will allow to adjust textures later inside the app - it somehow works as you can see in the video, but it is far from perfect. For smaller models in some isometric RPG it is fine, for detailed object you can examine up close - not so much. Once I figure out how to apply perfect texture on any model, there is no need to use online tools or bother Claude for your credit anymore.

  
Btw I also designed tool to make ingame music. There is keyboard, so the main melody is yours, tool will design drums and chords around it etc. Not great results and also needs a lot of tweaking, but again - better than just prompt it on some AI website and take whatever it creates.

  
Are you facing similar issues? What solution did you find?

comments.author: PulIthEld
comments.body:
All local, all open models, mostly glued together with Python and Blender scripts:

1. Concept: Z-Image Turbo in ComfyUI makes a front or three-quarter concept on a plain white background, lit flat so no lighting gets baked in.
2. Shape: the background is cut out with BiRefNet, then TripoSG turns the image into a mesh (~40–60k faces).
3. Texture: Marigold divides out whatever lighting is left in the image, then TRELLIS.2 textures the TripoSG mesh from that flattened image.
4. Finish (Blender):
   - stray pieces are dropped
   - remaining shading is removed with a spherical-harmonics fit
   - the model is scaled to size and set on its real base
   - textures are compressed to KTX2
5. Review: a small local web page shows every asset (concept, spinnable model) with approve / deny / "send back with notes". The notes go into a queue my coding agent watches, and it fixes and regenerates.

https://i.redd.it/ms8ldty0aiwh1.png

Special cases:
- Trees and plants: the shape model turns leaves into floating blobs, so those get deleted and replaced with alpha cards using a generated leaf-sprig photo.

- Creatures: auto-rigged by fitting an existing skeleton to the mesh, so they reuse existing animation clips.

- Characters and gear: the most work.

  - A generated base body is bound to the existing skeleton, with the skeleton moved onto the body's own joints.
 
 - Each armour piece is inpainted onto that body's own concept image, inside a mask of the slot's body regions, so it's drawn in the exact same pose.
 
 - It's then modelled, cut to the slot, carried onto the skeleton with the same per-vertex map as the body, and given the body's skin weights. Every piece fits every other piece without hand-fitting.

  - Simple things like rope belts are just built procedurally around the body's waist line.

Everything is packed into one texture atlas per body, so a whole character is still one draw call.

comments.author: W3103_

For me, Suno is worth it on the music front, like 8$ a month and you get hundreds and hundreds of generations, can download like 30 per month on lowest tier.

Lots of people give Suno flack because they can’t just type in ‘cool video game soundtrack, retro, ambient’ and get perfect sounds. Garbage prompts make garbage tracks

If you make hyper stylised prompts specific to what you’re after, if you know roughly what you’re looking for especially with the instruments you want to be used, for me - it is excellent. Plus if you have a tune in your head you can just hum or sing it into the mic and it’ll make a song with that tune - love it tbh
